title: Customers rely on the product, but [[a slow start and the price]] are costing recommendations
subtitle: What explains the scores, who is least happy, and what to do next.
answer: NPS is [[below zero]]. People who recommend us praise {{reliability}}. People who don't mostly struggled with onboarding or feel the price is too high, and small companies feel this most.

chapters.title: Onboarding and price matter most, and [[both score low]]
chapters.summary: Two items explain most of the difference in NPS, and only about a third rate them well.
chapters.lede: We measured how strongly each rating is linked to recommending us, and how many people rate it well.
chapters.so_what: Improving onboarding and how value is communicated is the change most likely to move NPS.

chapters.title: The smaller the company, [[the less likely they are to recommend us]]
chapters.summary: Companies of 1-10 people score far below companies of 250+.
chapters.so_what: Small companies trail on onboarding and value, not on reliability.

chapters.title: Three mindsets, and one is [[deeply unhappy]]
chapters.summary: About one in six people rate almost everything low.

chapters.title: In their own words, setup and price come up most
chapters.summary: Comments match the scores: setup and price are the main complaints.

chapters.title: Reliability is the only item most people rate well
chapters.summary: Every other experience item is rated well by fewer than half.

actions.text: Redesign first-week setup, starting with companies under 10 people.
Test a lighter plan for small teams.
Keep reliability where it is; it is what promoters praise.

next_questions.text: Why are small companies less likely to recommend us?
Which setup steps do unhappy customers mention most?
